title: Make install.sh put forgel-code on PATH for a new terminal
summary: The installer reports success while a new terminal cannot find forgel-code: the PATH block lands in a profile file the user's shell does not read on login and nothing verifies it. The change detects the real login shell, writes a duplicate-safe block into the files that shell reads, verifies the result in a fresh login shell with a loud failure message, and removes the block from every profile file on --uninstall.
requirements: Shell resolution never assumes bash. The detected login shell is, in order: $SHELL when it names a shell the installer handles (zsh, bash, sh, dash, ksh, ksh93, mksh, pdksh, ash, yash); otherwise the shell of the invoking process ancestry (the parent process, read with ps) when that names a handled shell; otherwise the account login shell (macOS `dscl . -read "$HOME" UserShell` first, then `getent passwd <uid>` or the /etc/passwd entry); otherwise /bin/sh. An empty or unset $SHELL must never by itself produce a bash decision.
When the detected shell is zsh, the block is written to ~/.zshrc, created when it does not exist.

When the detected shell is bash, the block is written to a file an interactive login bash reads: ~/.bash_profile when it exists; otherwise the first existing of ~/.bash_login and ~/.profile; when none of the three exists, ~/.bash_profile is created. The block is never written to ~/.bashrc alone.

When the detected shell is not zsh and not bash (the POSIX family, including the /bin/sh fallback and a shell the installer does not recognise), the block is written to ~/.profile and the installer prints a warning on stderr that names the edited file and the detected shell.
FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE, when set, replaces the selected profile file for both install and uninstall.

The written block is delimited by the marker lines `# >>> forgel-code >>>` and `# <<< forgel-code <<<`, compared byte for byte, and its body is a POSIX `case "$PATH:" in` guard that prepends the launcher directory to PATH only when that directory is not already present. No unguarded `export PATH=...` line is written.
Sourcing several profile files that each carry the block leaves exactly one occurrence of the launcher directory in PATH.

Unless the profile edit is opted out, after writing the block the installer starts the detected shell as a login shell from a cleared environment (`env -i` carrying only HOME, SHELL, TERM=dumb and PATH=/usr/bin:/bin, stdin from /dev/null), under a bounded time limit, and requires `command -v forgel-code` in that shell to resolve to the launcher path the installer wrote.

The bounded time limit must work on a host without GNU coreutils, so it cannot depend on the `timeout` binary alone; a portable watchdog that kills the shell and treats the result as a verification failure is required.
On verification failure the installer exits non-zero and prints, on stderr, the edited profile file, the exact block it wrote, the shell it checked and the PATH that shell reported.
On verification success the installer exits zero and prints the detected shell, the edited profile file and the path the fresh shell resolved.

When FORGEL_CODE_NO_MODIFY_PATH or FORGEL_CODE_NO_PROFILE_EDIT is set to an opt-out value, no profile file is opened for writing, no verification runs, the exact `export PATH="<bin dir>:$PATH"` line is printed and the installer exits zero.

--uninstall removes the marked block from every profile file the installer can write — ~/.zshrc, ~/.zprofile, ~/.zshenv, ~/.bash_profile, ~/.bash_login, ~/.profile, ~/.bashrc — and from FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE when it is set. It changes no other line of those files, creates no missing file, and exits zero when a file is absent or carries no marker.
Running the installer twice leaves exactly one marked block in the selected profile file and exactly one occurrence of the launcher directory in PATH.
The script stays POSIX sh: `sh -n install.sh` succeeds under dash, and the script never reads stdin, so `curl ... | sh` and `sh < install.sh` work.

Existing behaviour is preserved: installation from a local checkout with FORGEL_CODE_SOURCE and without network, installation into FORGEL_CODE_HOME and the launcher into FORGEL_CODE_BIN, no virtualenv, `forgel-code --version` printing `forgel-code <version>`, and the opt-out variables.

tests/test_install.py gains passing cases named (or selected by a -k expression matching) zsh without $SHELL, bash with an existing ~/.bash_profile, bash with a missing ~/.bash_profile, unknown shell, the duplicate-safe guard when several profiles are sourced, failing verification, repeated install, --uninstall cleanup, and installation through a shell reading install.sh from stdin.
No existing test in tests/ is deleted or loosened; tests that assert the exact block text are updated to the guarded block.

README.md's Install, Options, Update and Uninstall text matches the resulting behaviour (guarded block, warning for an unrecognised shell, the verification and its failure report, the profile list) and names no step the installer no longer requires; tests/test_readme_install.py still passes.

external_dependencies.name: macOS Directory Service `dscl`
external_dependencies.interface: On macOS the real `dscl . -read "$HOME" UserShell` prints `UserShell: <path>` and the installer parses the path. It is not present on Linux CI, so the suite substitutes a deterministic stub selected through FORGEL_STUB_USER_SHELL (tests/test_install.py DSCL_STUB contract); the installer code path is unchanged, only the executable is replaced by the stub on PATH.
external_dependencies.docs: dscl(1); stub contract recorded in tests/test_install.py (DSCL_STUB)
external_dependencies.evidence: Specification dependency entry: 'dscl . -read "$HOME" UserShell' prints 'UserShell: <path>'; the rest of the suite may stub it through FORGEL_STUB_USER_SHELL as tests/test_install.py already records (DSCL_STUB). dscl exists only on macOS and is therefore not callable directly in this environment.
external_dependencies.stub:
#!/bin/sh
# Deterministic dscl stub (DSCL_STUB contract).
# Emulates: dscl . -read "$HOME" UserShell  ->  "UserShell: <path>"
# The login shell is supplied by FORGEL_STUB_USER_SHELL.

if [ "$1" != "." ] || [ "$2" != "-read" ] || [ -z "$3" ]; then
    echo "dscl stub: unsupported invocation: $*" >&2
    exit 64
fi

case "$4" in
    UserShell|'') ;;
    *)
        echo "dscl stub: unsupported attribute: $4" >&2
        exit 64
        ;;
esac

if [ -z "${FORGEL_STUB_USER_SHELL:-}" ]; then
    echo "dscl stub: FORGEL_STUB_USER_SHELL is not set" >&2
    exit 1
fi

printf 'UserShell: %s\n' "$FORGEL_STUB_USER_SHELL"
exit 0

external_dependencies.name: passwd database (`getent`, /etc/passwd)
external_dependencies.interface: Login-shell lookup when $SHELL is empty and dscl is unavailable: `getent passwd <uid>` and, as fallback, the /etc/passwd line for the uid; field 7 is the login shell.
external_dependencies.evidence: Specification dependency entry: `getent passwd <uid>` or the /etc/passwd line for the uid, field 7 is the login shell. `getent` and /etc/passwd are local facilities present in the environment contract for a Linux sandbox (environment/Dockerfile, environment.yaml).

external_dependencies.name: ps
external_dependencies.interface: Parent/login process fallback for the invoking user's shell: `ps -p <pid> -o comm=` (BSD and GNU both accept -o comm=), with basename normalisation so `/bin/sh` maps to sh; used when $SHELL is empty and no account database entry is usable.
external_dependencies.evidence: Specification dependency entry: `ps -p <pid> -o comm=` (BSD and GNU both accept -o comm=) to read the parent process command for the parent-shell fallback; the output may need basename normalisation. ps is a locally installed executable (procps/BSD base).

external_dependencies.name: GNU coreutils `timeout` (optional)
external_dependencies.interface: Optional bound on the verification shell: `timeout <seconds> <shell> -l -i -c '<command>'` when `timeout` is on PATH; when absent the installer must use a portable background-and-kill watchdog instead, so `timeout` is never a hard requirement.
external_dependencies.evidence: Specification dependency entry: used when present to bound the verification shell; when absent the installer must fall back to a portable background-and-kill watchdog. Must not be a hard requirement. GNU coreutils timeout is the local executable used when available.

result.summary: Restored the four installer tests the review flagged as unjustifiably deleted, so tests/test_install.py again carries the originally present install-path cases in addition to the new ones, and left install.sh and README.md untouched because they already implement the specification (login-shell resolution, guarded marked block, bounded fresh-shell verification with its failure report, full --uninstall cleanup). test_profile_the_login_shell_ignores_fails_verification puts the block in ~/.bashrc, which a login /bin/sh never reads, and asserts a non-zero exit with the file, block, shell and PATH on stderr; test_second_run_is_idempotent runs the installer twice and asserts the profile is byte-identical with one marker and no unguarded export; test_piped_install_does_not_read_the_script_from_stdin feeds install.sh plus a trailing line to `sh` on stdin and asserts the trailing line still runs; test_unset_shell_puts_the_block_in_zshrc runs the installer without SHELL through an interpreter that does not re-assign SHELL and asserts the block lands in ~/.zshrc via the account login shell. The unset-SHELL case needed a host-independent launcher: a shell that assigns SHELL at startup (bash on this host) hid the unset state, so the test selects an interpreter that keeps SHELL unset and skips with an explicit reason when none is installed. Verified with `python -m pytest -q tests/test_install.py` (40 passed, 51s), the four targeted cases alone (4 passed), and the full suite `python -m pytest -q` (188 passed, 137 subtests passed, 89s). No test was weakened or deleted.

review.summary: The attributed change implements the specification faithfully. install.sh now resolves the login shell in the required order ($SHELL, then the invoking process via ps, then the account login shell via dscl/getent/passwd, then /bin/sh), selects the profile an interactive login session of that shell actually reads (zsh → ~/.zshrc, bash → first existing of ~/.bash_profile/~/.bash_login/~/.profile or a created ~/.bash_profile, POSIX family → ~/.profile with a stderr warning naming shell and file), writes a byte-delimited block whose body is a POSIX `case ":$PATH:"` guard instead of an unguarded export, verifies the result in a cleared login interactive shell under a portable background-watchdog bound that needs no GNU timeout and maps a kill to exit status 124, and reports failures with the edited file, the exact block, the checked shell and the PATH that shell saw. Uninstall covers every writable profile plus FORGEL_CODE_PROFILE without creating or altering other lines, the opt-out path still prints the plain export line and skips verification, and the script stays POSIX sh with stdin redirected to /dev/null on every child. README.md matches the new behaviour (guarded block, unrecognised-shell warning, bounded verification and its failure report, the full uninstall profile list) without adding a step the installer no longer needs. The recorded dscl stub in tests/test_install.py answers the exact invocation the installer makes (`dscl . -read <home> UserShell` → `UserShell: <path>`), so it does not contradict the recorded dependency. No test removals were detected and the full suite plus the dash parse check pass. Two non-blocking observations: the watchdog uses a predictable name under ${TMPDIR:-/tmp} that is truncated with `: >`, a low-severity local symlink race, and tests/_timing_probe.py was committed and then dropped inside this task's history, so it is absent from the final tree and leaves no stale test behind.
